entities.name: Lucius Titinius Pansa Saccus
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Lucius Titinius Pansa Saccus was a Roman politician and consul in the late Republic period, born to a wealthy family of consular rank.

As a prominent figure during this tumultuous era, he played a key role in the First Triumvirate, serving as a close ally to Julius Caesar and Marcus Licinius Crassus. His involvement in the civil war that followed the assassination of Julius Caesar led to his eventual downfall and death at the hands of Brutus.

Pansa's legacy is often overshadowed by that of his contemporaries, but his actions had significant repercussions on the Roman state, contributing to its gradual transformation into the imperial system.

In the annals of Roman history, Pansa's story serves as a poignant reminder of the treacherous nature of politics and the devastating consequences of ambition.
